title: "Research"

My research explores connections between quantum gravity, holography, geometry, gauge theory, and mathematical physics.

## Spectral Holography

**MSci Research Project, University of Nottingham**

*Emergent Geometry, Gauge Theory, and Gravity from Modular Graph Entanglement*

**Overview**

A spectral framework connecting weighted graphs, operator algebras, modular structure, gauge holonomies, and emergent geometry. The project investigates how geometric and gravitational structures can arise from underlying spectral and entanglement data.

**Motivation**

The project is motivated by the possibility that spacetime geometry is emergent rather than fundamental. It asks whether geometric information can be reconstructed from more primitive algebraic, spectral, and quantum data.

[Project PDF →](Spectral_Holography%20copy.pdf)

## The Universal York Hamiltonian

**Independent Research Project**

*An Exact Scaling Law for Constant-Mean-Curvature Time in AdS3 Gravity, and a Stress-Tensor Dilation Law on its Boundary*

**Overview**

A study of York time and Hamiltonian evolution in three-dimensional AdS gravity. The project develops an exact scaling law for the York Hamiltonian in constant-mean-curvature time and investigates the corresponding dilation law for the boundary stress tensor.

**Motivation**

The project is motivated by the role of time and polarization in gravitational phase space. York time provides a geometric choice of clock through constant-mean-curvature foliations, giving a setting in which bulk Hamiltonian evolution can be related to boundary conformal data.

[Project PDF →](york_time%20%281%29.pdf)


## Iterated Conformal Infinity Is Not Iterated Holography

**Independent Research Project**

*Depth-Two Conformal Infinity, Cornered Geometry, and the Limits of Recursive Holography*

**Overview**

A geometric study of “depth-two” conformal infinity, where a conformal boundary itself carries asymptotically hyperbolic structure. The project shows how this naturally leads to cornered geometry, while distinguishing nested conformal structure from a genuinely recursive holographic duality.

**Motivation**

The project is motivated by the question of whether holography can be iterated, with a boundary itself becoming a new bulk. The analysis identifies a representative-selection obstruction: conformal infinity determines a conformal class rather than a distinguished asymptotically hyperbolic representative. This separates nested geometry from genuine iterated holography and points toward relative or defect sectors.

[Project PDF →](nested_holography%20%281%29.pdf)

## Hodge-Relative Completions of Characteristic Brane Couplings

**Independent Research Project**

**Overview**

This project studies metric-dependent completions of characteristic brane couplings using differential forms, characteristic classes, and the Hodge operator. It explores how characteristic and topological data can be extended into structures carrying local field-theoretic information.

**Motivation**

The starting point is a contrast with Chern–Simons theory. Chern–Simons constructions naturally encode global and topological information from local gauge fields. Here the question is reversed: can global characteristic data be completed using the Hodge operator so that local physical structure becomes visible?

[Project PDF →](Hodge_relative_completions_of_characteristic_brane_couplings%20%283%29.pdf)

## Strain as Curvature

**Independent Research Project**

**Overview**

This project identifies a distinguished geometric sector of the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations through the $SO(3)$ decomposition of the velocity gradient. The transverse-traceless strain sector corresponds to helicity $\pm 2$ and admits a curvature interpretation for the effective metric $g=\delta+2S$.

The project also connects material deformation to $SL(3,\mathbb{R})/SO(3)$ and studies the global topology of this geometric sector.

**Motivation**

The aim is to place fluid strain, curvature, representation theory, and topology within a common geometric framework. Existing Navier–Stokes regularity criteria are reinterpreted in this setting, without claiming a new regularity theorem.

[Project PDF →](Strain_as_Curvature%20%281%29.pdf)
